## Description {#details}

A class template for a doubly linked list of nodes.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">Type of the elements linked into the list, derived from class <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links-base">double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base</Link></code>.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="L">Type of the links node (either <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links">double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code> or <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/static-double-list-links">static&#95;double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code>).</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>
This class implements a generic doubly linked list, maintaining a pair of head and tail pointers to allow efficient iteration and manipulation of nodes. The list elements (of type T) must be derived from <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links-base">double&#95;list&#95;links&#95;base</Link></code> (typically from <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links">double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code>) and extended with the required payload, which may be the actual content or a pointer to it.

The class uses composition for the links node, rather than inheritance, to avoid inheriting unwanted methods. Iterators return pointers to the list elements, enabling traversal of the list in a manner similar to standard containers.


:::info
Only forward iterators are provided by default, but reverse iterators can be added if required.
:::

## Protected Member Attributes

### links&#95; {#a22d5f70c0589acc1c18d10e740c7a599}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class L = double&#95;list&#95;links&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>links&#95;type micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&lt; T, L &gt;::links&#95;</>}
  labels = {["protected"]}>
The list top node used to point to <b>head</b> and <b>tail</b> nodes.

This member stores the internal links node for the list. The <b>next</b> pointer of this node points to the head of the list, and the <b>previous</b> pointer points to the tail. For an empty list, both pointers refer to the node itself, simplifying list management and boundary checks.

## Public Constructors

### double&#95;list() {#aae4f864990bb22d349fc6f4fe06978fa}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class L = double&#95;list&#95;links&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&lt; T, L &gt;::double&#95;list ()</>}>
Construct a doubly linked list.

For non-statically allocated lists, the initial list status is <em>empty</em> after construction, meaning the list is ready for use and contains no nodes.

For statically allocated lists, the list remains <em>uninitialised</em> after construction, with its internal pointers set to <code>nullptr</code>. Such lists require explicit initialisation (typically via <code><Link to="#a6c5ca2deb541088fac9aae237e0c3699">initialize&#95;once()</Link></code>) before use.

This constructor does not clear or modify the internal pointers for statically allocated lists, relying on zero-initialisation by the runtime. For dynamically allocated lists, it calls <code><Link to="#ab19a62873a09745075bdceb60096c03c">clear()</Link></code> to ensure the list is in a valid empty state.


<SectionUser title="The rule of five">
The copy constructor, move constructor, copy assignment operator, and move assignment operator are explicitly deleted to prevent accidental copying or moving of <Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/intrusive-list">intrusive&#95;list</Link> objects. This ensures the integrity of the list structure, as duplicating or moving lists could result in invalid or inconsistent links within the list.
</SectionUser>

### ~double&#95;list() {#a9eba8d60614723f1c041359fe8d9f4bd}

Destruct the list.

Normally at this point there must be no nodes in the list. However, for statically allocated lists, this might not be always true due to their lifetime and initialization patterns.

### begin() {#acf7950853947782be95524ffe30febef}

<MemberDefinition

Iterator begin.

<SectionUser title="Returns">
An iterator to the first element.
</SectionUser>

Returns an iterator to the first element in the list. For statically allocated lists, asserts that the list is already initialised. The iterator will point to the node after the internal links node (the head). If the list is empty, the iterator will compare equal to <code><Link to="#abb4f476badf26d59503fe5a3a2ad0400">end()</Link></code>.

</SectionUser>

The <code><Link to="#ab19a62873a09745075bdceb60096c03c">clear()</Link></code> method initialises the mandatory internal links node so that both its <code>previous&#95;</code> and <code>next&#95;</code> pointers refer to itself. This marks the list as empty and ensures it is in a safe, known state, ready for new insertions. This operation is typically used to reset the list, removing all elements and breaking any existing links.
